home.a2Title: What makes it A2 — and why that matters
home.a2Body: Ordinary milk carries a mix of A1 and A2 beta-casein protein. When A1 is digested it releases BCM-7, a peptide linked to bloating and discomfort in people who are sensitive to it. Milk from desi cows and from all buffaloes is A2 only — no BCM-7. People who feel heavy after regular milk often find A2 sits easier.

ourMilk.a2SectionTitle: A1, A2 and BCM-7 — in plain words
a2Paras: About 30% of the protein in milk is beta-casein. It comes in two main forms, A1 and A2, that differ by a single amino acid at one position in the chain.

When your body digests the A1 form, it releases a fragment called beta-casomorphin-7 (BCM-7). In people who are sensitive to it, BCM-7 has been linked in trials to bloating, softer stools and general gut discomfort. The A2 form does not release BCM-7.

Indigenous humped cattle — Sahiwal, Gir, Rathi, Tharparkar — mostly carry only the A2 gene. High-yield crossbred and exotic cows often carry A1. All buffalo milk is A2, because buffaloes do not carry the A1 gene at all.

This is why many people who feel heavy or bloated after ordinary milk can drink A2 comfortably. It is a digestion difference, not a cure — A2 milk still contains lactose, and we make no claims about disease.
ourMilk.nutritionBody: Buffalo milk is naturally higher in protein, fat and calcium than cow milk — with no fortification. A 250 ml glass of our buffalo milk is roughly 9–11 g of complete protein.
ourMilk.nutritionFoot: Indicative ranges for whole, unprocessed milk; exact values vary by animal, season and feed.

ourFarm.title: Our Farm
ourFarm.intro: We keep two indigenous dairy breeds and raise them the way that keeps their milk clean and A2 — on land you are welcome to visit.
sahiwalBody: The Sahiwal is India's finest indigenous dairy cow, from the Sahiwal tract of the Punjab. Reddish-brown with loose skin, it tolerates heat and ticks, stays calm and healthy on green fodder, and needs little input.

A well-kept Sahiwal gives about 8–12 litres a day, with butterfat around 4.5–5%. Genetically it is A2A2 at the beta-casein gene — which is the whole reason we keep Sahiwals rather than high-yield crossbreds.
murrahBody: The Murrah is the world's benchmark dairy buffalo, from Haryana — jet-black, with tightly coiled horns. It is exported around the world to improve buffalo herds.

A Murrah gives roughly 8–16 litres a day, with butterfat around 7% and very high total solids — that is what makes buffalo milk thick and rich. All buffalo milk is naturally A2; buffaloes do not carry the A1 gene.

practices.d: A steady diet of green fodder and farm-made silage — nutritious feed that keeps the animals healthy and the milk consistent through the year.
Our animals live on the farm under our care. No roadside grazing, no stray cattle mixed into the herd.
A weekly herbal health routine to support immunity and keep the animals well — prevention before treatment.
We never use hormones or yield-boosting injections. Nothing that does not belong in milk goes into our animals.
Milked every day and moved quickly to delivery — not stored, not pooled from many sources.
From milking to the bottle at your door, the milk is checked at each stage. Zero water mixed, nothing added, nothing removed.

ourFarm.visitBody: Trust is easier when you can see the farm. If you would like to visit before you subscribe, ask on the order page and we will arrange it.

items.q: What does A2 milk actually mean?
items.a: It refers to the type of beta-casein protein in the milk. A2 milk has only the A2 form, so it does not release BCM-7 during digestion. Milk from our Sahiwal cows and Murrah buffaloes is naturally A2.
No. A2 milk still contains lactose. A2 is about the protein, not the sugar. If you are lactose intolerant, A2 milk will not change that.

items.q: Is buffalo milk better than cow milk?
items.a: Neither is 'better' — they are different. Buffalo milk is thicker and higher in protein, fat and calcium; cow milk is lighter and easier for some people to drink daily. Many families take both.

items.q: Do you add anything to the milk?
items.a: No. Nothing is added and nothing is removed. No water, no preservatives, no powder. It is whole milk exactly as it comes from the animal, after filtering and a quality check.

items.q: How do I place an order?
items.a: Use the order page. Fill the short form, choose cow milk, buffalo milk or both, and how often you want it. It opens WhatsApp with your order ready to send; the farm confirms your delivery slot.
You can pay by UPI or after delivery. For a running subscription, the farm shares a monthly amount that you can pay by UPI.

items.q: Can I pause or change my subscription?
items.a: Yes. From My Account you can pause for a holiday, skip a day, change the quantity, or switch between cow and buffalo milk at any time.

items.q: Which areas do you deliver to?
items.a: Delivery areas are confirmed when you order. Enter your area and pincode on the order form and the farm will tell you the delivery slot for your locality.
